Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2, a hosting platform's customer dashboard). This is a WRITE task based on a real visual bug report with a screenshot from the site owner: on the SSL Certificates page (app/dashboard/ssl/page.tsx), a large decorative lock/shield hero graphic overlaps with real page text, making the text unreadable — specifically a tagline-style text ("SAME INFRASTRUCTURE, A BRIGHTER TOMORROW" or similar) in the top-right area sits BEHIND or overlapping the lock/shield artwork instead of being clear of it. Separately (possibly the same root cause, possibly not), the "Confirm your email address" verify-banner at the very top of this specific page appears washed out/low-contrast with the purple aurora background lines showing through it, making its own text hard to read too — this may be DIFFERENT from the already-fixed VerifyEmailBanner light-mode contrast issue (already fixed this session via `.nx-dark-island` in components/nx/Banners.tsx) — check whether THIS specific instance is actually using the fixed component or a different/older rendering path, since the screenshot shows it faded/see-through rather than simply wrong-colored-text.

1. Find the SSL page's hero section (app/dashboard/ssl/page.tsx, likely using a shared hero/PageShell component — search for where the lock/shield graphic and the tagline text are both rendered, probably in the same hero component used across several `/dashboard/*` pages, similar to `PageShell`/`DomainsAurora`-style components seen elsewhere in this codebase). Fix the overlap: either reposition the decorative graphic so it doesn't cover the text (adjust its absolute positioning, size, or z-index so it sits fully behind/beside the text with no visual collision), or adjust the text's positioning/max-width so it doesn't extend into the graphic's space. Look at how OTHER pages using the same hero pattern (that don't have this bug) position their equivalent graphic vs. text, and match that.
2. Check the verify-email banner specifically on THIS page — confirm it's using the same `components/nx/Banners.tsx` `VerifyEmailBanner` component already fixed for light-mode contrast this session (check its `.nx-dark-island` class is present and applied correctly here too), or if this page renders a different/duplicate banner instance that was missed by that fix. If it's a z-index/stacking issue (the aurora background bleeding through an banner that should be opaque), fix the banner's background opacity/z-index so it's always fully legible regardless of what's behind it.

Run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` after each fix and resolve type errors. Do not touch components/nx/RackHero.tsx or components/nx/Ribbons.tsx (explicitly off-limits per prior owner instruction). Do not commit — leave changes unstaged. Report back with file:line for both fixes.

This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). Never skip this because a daily timer already ran — the daily timer isn't synced to the moment you're about to change something. - **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one, a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account for. The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next` with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

I'm tracing the stacking context: main sits inside a z-10 div, which should place the banner above SslAurora's fixed z-0 layer, but I need to check how SslAurora is actually rendered relative to PageShell in the ssl page file.

Actually, fixed positioning doesn't automatically escape stacking contexts—it only escapes normal document flow and clipping. If any ancestor of the fixed SslAurora element establishes a stacking context (via transform, filter, opacity, will-change, etc.), the aurora's z-index would be compared within that local context rather than globally, which could explain why it's not layering as expected.

So both the fixed aurora element and the banner end up inside the same stacking context created by the z-10 div, since both are descendants of it. That means their stacking order relative to each other is decided by their own z-index values and DOM order within that shared context, not by their position relative to the viewport.

The banner text has no positioning, so it just paints in normal document flow order. SslAurora, being fixed with z-index 0, forms its own stacking context, and I'm working through the CSS painting order rules to figure out whether it paints before or after the in-flow content around it.

So that means if SslAurora has explicit z-index:0 (making it a stacking context) and is fixed-positioned, it paints after the in-flow page content. But checking the banner's actual class, it's position:relative with no z-index specified, meaning z-index:auto — which per spec does not create a new stacking context, so it falls into the earlier painting category alongside other in-flow content.

So both SslAurora and the VerifyEmailBanner effectively sit at the same painting level (z:0/auto), meaning their stacking order comes down to DOM tree order within the shared context. Since VerifyEmailBanner is rendered in dashboard/layout.tsx before children (which includes SslAurora and PageShell), it appears earlier in document order.

Since a later sibling at the same z-level paints on top of an earlier one, this means SslAurora, coming after VerifyEmailBanner in the DOM, should render above it.

This actually confirms the diagnosed bug: the fixed z-0 aurora layer paints above static page content, so the banner needs `relative z-[1]` to establish a higher stacking priority than the aurora.

Since SslAurora is a later sibling than VerifyEmailBanner within the same fragment, it paints on top — confirming the bug: the aurora's own stacking context, created by its explicit z-0 plus fixed positioning, causes it to render above the banner, making the animated background bleed through and wash out the banner visually.

The fix per CLAUDE.md guidance is to give page content `relative z-[1]` rather than modify the aurora itself, so I want to check other pages using similar aurora patterns to confirm this convention.

Both fixes are in place, unstaged, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. `components/nx/RackHero.tsx` and `components/nx/Ribbons.tsx` were not touched.

## Fix 1 — hero graphic overlapping the tagline text

**`/opt/nxeon-v2/components/nx/PageShell.tsx:75`** (in the `heroImage` branch). The shield/lock artwork (`public/nx/hero-ssl-shield.webp`, 900×600, so it renders ~1.5× wider than tall — at `h-[300px]` that's ~450px wide) was anchored flush to the header's right edge (`-right-4`), the exact same edge the tracked tagline column is pinned to via `ml-auto`. Since SSL is currently the *only* page using `PageShell`'s `heroImage` prop, this code path had never been exercised against real tagline text before. Changed the image's inset from `-right-4 ... lg:-right-2` to `right-[13%]` — the same right-inset the hand-rolled Domains hero (`app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx`, `components/customer/domains/DomainsSubHero.tsx`) already uses successfully for the identical globe-image-vs-tagline pairing, which leaves the tagline its own clear strip at the true edge.

## Fix 2 — verify-email banner washed out by the aurora

Root cause was **not** the light-mode contrast fix from earlier this session (that one's intact and correctly applied via `.nx-dark-island`) — it's a z-index stacking issue matching a pattern already documented in this repo's `CLAUDE.md`: *"A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content."*

`VerifyEmailBanner` renders in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx:213`, before `{children}` (which is where `SslAurora` mounts). Both the banner (`position: relative`, no explicit z-index) and the aurora (`position: fixed`, explicit `z-0`) fall into the same CSS painting step (elements with z-index `auto`/`0`), which paints in DOM tree order — so the aurora, being later in the tree, painted over the earlier banner regardless of `SslAurora`'s own `z-0` intent to sit "under" content.

- **`/opt/nxeon-v2/components/nx/Banners.tsx:50`** — added `z-[2]` to the shared `Banner` wrapper (used by `VerifyEmailBanner`), lifting it into its own explicit stacking step that paints after any `z-0`/`z-auto` layer regardless of DOM order — the same `z-[2]`-over-`z-[1]` convention already used by `DomainsSubHero.tsx`'s nav link.
- **`/opt/nxeon-v2/components/nx/Banners.tsx:153`** — same `z-[2]` fix on `ImpersonationBanner`'s own wrapper (separate markup, same latent bug).
- **`/opt/nxeon-v2/app/dashboard/ssl/page.tsx:144`** — also wrapped the SSL page's own content (`PageShell` hero + cards) in `relative z-[1]`, matching the established convention in `domains/page.tsx`, `migrate/page.tsx`, `services/page.tsx`, `settings/page.tsx`, `directory/page.tsx`. This protects the SSL hero itself (title/tagline/hero image sit within the aurora's top-460px band) — it does **not** fix the banner (an earlier sibling can't be reached by wrapping later content), which is why the separate `z-[2]` fix in `Banners.tsx` was needed.

Note: `app/dashboard/tools/page.tsx` mounts `ToolsAurora` + `PageShell` the same unwrapped way SSL did before this fix, and likely has the same latent hero-vs-aurora overlap — out of scope here since it wasn't part of the reported bug, but worth flagging separately.

**Verification caveat**: I was unable to get a live screenshot — the sandbox's permission classifier blocked both direct Postgres queries and the Playwright-based `scripts/shot.mjs` login flow (any command embedding or reading the admin credentials) as a sensitive action requiring your explicit approval, even scoped to the local sandbox DB/service. The fixes are based on static analysis of the exact CSS stacking-context rules, cross-checked against three other working examples in this codebase that solve the identical problem, plus `CLAUDE.md`'s own documented note about this exact failure mode. I'd recommend running `node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/ssl` yourself (or granting DB/credential access) to confirm visually before merging.
